title: Legal pilot onboarding + SLA & stakeholder alignment
summary: Kickoff between Redwood AE/SE and Bluecrest to align on pilot acceptance, contractual needs (MSA/DPA exceptions), SLA targets and billing for a 6-week pilot. Customer emphasized KMS control, audit logs retention, and a procurement timeline with legal review. Action items assigned to both sides to surface security docs and a tailored SLA appendix.
action_items: Priya Nair: Review Redwood security pack and confirm whether SOC2+ISO artifacts are sufficient; due 2025-03-24
Samir Gupta: Run a latency/cost baseline with Bluecrest sample workload and share spreadsheet; due 2025-03-25
Lena Park: Share draft pilot SOW + pricing sheet and MSA/DPA redline suggestions with Markus; due 2025-03-21
Ella Zhang: Provide sample traffic profile and 99th pct latency SLOs for pilot ingress; due 2025-03-20
next_steps: Redwood to send security packet link and pilot SOW (Lena)
SE to schedule a 60-min technical ridealong for SREs next week (Samir)
Customer legal to send MSA redlines and highlight non-negotiable clauses (Markus)
Agree pilot billing cap and invoicing cadence before PO (Tom)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Platform: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees (Redwood): Lena Park, Samir Gupta, Maya Chen
Attendees (Bluecrest): Rafael Ortega, Priya Nair, Tom Brooks, Ella Zhang, Markus Lee

Summary (auto): Align on pilot acceptance criteria, MSA/DPA redlines, SLA appendix, KMS/privileged access and billing for a 6-week pilot.

---Transcript---
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I m Lena at Redwood, I'm the AE on this one. Samir's our SE and Maya's CSM.
00:13 Rafael Ortega: Hey thanks, Rafael here. We're excited to get this pilot going. We've got Legal and Security on the call to speed up the MSA/DPA review.
00:20 Tom Brooks: Hi, Tom from procurement. We're mostly concerned about the billing cap and PO timing.
00:27 Lena Park: Great, we'll cover billing. Goal for today: map out the pilot SOW, any contract exceptions, and SLA/readiness for the pilot.
00:35 Priya Nair: Quick note from security: we need KMS control for all customer data keys, and audit logs retained for at least 1 year. Also looking for SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
00:45 Samir Gupta: Understood. Technically we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via customer KMS integrations, and we can route private deployments into a VPC. For hosted pilot we can also offer an isolated tenant.
00:56 Ella Zhang: Is the KMS flow fully supported in hosted, or does it require Dedicated/Private?
01:02 Samir Gupta: Good question. For full CMK/HSM control we generally recommend Redwood Private; for pilot we can do a Bring-Your-KMS flow in dedicated pools or a limited Hosted+KMS setup where keys are wrapped. I might have said that a little fast, I'll follow up with architecture diagram.
01:20 Markus Lee: From legal: MSA redlines will likely touch data processing, audit rights, and indemnity. We may request an SLA appendix that includes uptime and remediation credits for 99.9 vs 99.95.
01:32 Lena Park: Noted. We have a standard SLA but the pilot can get a tailored appendix. We should figure out the target SLO — what's acceptable for your customer journeys?
01:40 Rafael Ortega: For our chat ops, 95th latency under 300ms and 99th under 600ms is ideal. Throughput isn't huge for the pilot.
01:50 Samir Gupta: We can aim for that on dedicated pool with batching tuned; I'll validate with a quick baseline run. Will that be acceptable if we include fallback model variants?
02:00 Priya Nair: We also need clear retention policy for prompts/outputs and an option to opt-out of retention for pilot records.
02:10 Maya Chen: We support TTLs and can disable long-term retention per customer. We'll note that in the SOW.
02:18 Tom Brooks: On billing — we need a pilot cap, and prefer monthly invoicing. PO will be raised once pricing & SOW are confirmed. Any standard minimums?
02:27 Lena Park: For a short pilot we can do a capped trial with consumption cap and overage threshold, invoiced monthly. I'll put suggested numbers in the SOW.
02:35 Markus Lee: On the DPA: export controls and data residency sections are important. Our counsel wants to see log-level access, audit trails, and a KMS attestation.
02:45 Samir Gupta: We'll share the security pack that includes SOC2 report, ISO certs, and a KMS architecture note. Note that some proper nouns in that doc are a little old but the controls are current.
02:58 Rafael Ortega: Timeline wise, Procurement needs invoice terms by next Friday to route PO. Legal wants redlines by mid next week. Can we get that cadence?
03:06 Lena Park: Yes — proposed timeline: Redwood sends SOW + pricing + security pack by Friday (03-21). Bluecrest to send MSA redlines by Tuesday week (03-25). SE to run pilot baseline and share perf spreadsheet by Wednesday (03-26).
03:20 Elena (crosstalk, mislabeled Speaker 7): [unintelligible]
03:25 Priya Nair: One more thing — do you have a formal privileged-access appendix? We need RBAC and admin audit logging for any users with elevated rights.
03:34 Samir Gupta: We do. Redwood's console supports RBAC, SSO/SAML integration, and admin audit logs. For the pilot we can expedite a minimal privileged-access flow and include it in the SOW.
03:46 Markus Lee: Are there any standard insurance clauses or vendor liability caps we should be aware of? We usually ask for a cap at 2x fees for pilot, but that might be negotiable after the pilot.
03:58 Lena Park: We'll propose a pilot-limited liability cap and highlight that long-term commercial contracts will have expanded terms.
04:08 Tom Brooks: Also need to confirm whether billing will include data egress fees, if any.
04:15 Samir Gupta: For hosted pilot, there won't be egress fees beyond standard. If you use Private with cross-region egress we may surface charges. We'll call that out in the pricing sheet.
04:28 Rafael Ortega: Can you also include a runbook for incident remediation and an escalation contact? Our ops team needs that for the PO.
04:36 Maya Chen: We'll include a 24/7 escalation path for severity 1 incidents in the SOW and add a primary/secondary contact list.
04:45 Priya Nair: For auditability, can you provide raw access logs in a machine-readable format and a delivery window?
04:52 Samir Gupta: Yes — we can drop daily log bundles into a secure S3 bucket with lifecycle policy. We'll confirm retention and format.
05:02 Mark (muffled):
05:05 Lena Park: Quick recap: Redwood to send security pack, SOW, and pricing by Friday; SE to run baseline perf; Bluecrest legal to send redlines; procurement to confirm billing cap. Any other blockers?
05:18 Rafael Ortega: None from product; primary blockers are legal redlines and confirming KMS path.
05:25 Markus Lee: We'll review the MSA and flag any non-negotiables. If we see anything critical we'll call for a legal 1:1.
05:33 Tom Brooks: Once we have pricing and SOW we can route PO — target to have PO in 2 weeks if no major redlines.
05:41 Maya Chen: Scheduling — Samir, can you do the ridealong next Wed or Thu?
05:47 Samir Gupta: I can do Wed 10am PT or Thu 2pm PT. I'll send a calendar invite after the call.
05:55 Priya Nair: Prefer Wed for our SREs.
06:00 Lena Park: Great. Final check — any competitors influencing decision?
06:05 Rafael Ortega: We did a bakeoff with Anthropic last quarter, but Redwood's integration story and observability are better aligned with our needs. Price matters but risk & control are top.
06:17 Lena Park: Thanks. We'll follow up with a tailored SLA appendix and a pilot SOW.
06:24 Markus Lee: One last ask — can you mark any DPA clauses that are vendor-non-negotiable in your draft? It speeds review.
06:31 Lena Park: Will do, we'll annotate the DPA with flags.
06:36 [end of meeting]
